The forecast implies that one of the unsolved Millennium Prize Problems most likely won't be solved by the first two deadlines unless an unprecedented breakthrough occurs. Nonetheless, having reliable models for solving hard mathematical problems would be a necessary step toward a solution of any open unsolved problem in any domain, where increments of now known to be infeasible problems are readily broken into components that are in principle tractable. The forecast sets the situation just prior to this necessary advance being realized.

The Hodge conjecture was solved, but the solution needs more elaboration before being accepted by the Clay Mathematics Institute existing solution by the forecast date. Abel, Krivine, Ysrael, Hyafil, and Halldórsson achieve the breakthrough in 2031, prior to December 31, 2035: Third deadline. The reward is awarded by the deadline
Given that neural networks, like classification trees, may have very little resemblance to the natural phenomenon they describe, having models capable of distinguishing Euler characteristic and efficient regular decompositions from singular ones with effective cohomology is the Hallmark of a quantum leap in the science and engineering of very large models.

A 2041 investigation attempts to solve the P versus NP problem by partitioning the solution space by cliques given the Bell inequality violation of 2.99, linearizing the mononotonous polynomial Boolean function into a linear system allowing completion via triangle-free decomposition, and determining the thermodynamic threshold boolean constraint k-clause SAT unsatisfiability by the phase transition. 1.13 P ≠ NP is established, but the existence of an O(n^(log log n)) PTAS for NP-complete problems remains unknown. The 2041 solution requires advent of the (FTI) policy of a Chinese First Team International deciding on the nationalization of the US Naval Observatory, and subsequent military and political clashes in the media, stealth cores of which involve quantum simulators of sufficiently large polynomial systems with essential complexity. Mathematical classification of the adequacy of quantum fingerprints requires identifying the inoherent ground states intractable through Landauer threshold dynamics.

The fact that the P versus NP conjecture was solved a year before the computer proposal was made suggests that P coincides with NP due to a fundamental symmetry irreducible to decision about the Church-Turing thesis
formatted_prompt:
Forecast date: 2025-04-29. Make a forecast from this date. Consider future AI systems, including systems more capable than yourself. Use your existing knowledge.

Forecast target: At least one of the six Millennium Prize Problems that were open at the forecast date: Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture, Hodge conjecture, Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness, P versus NP, Riemann hypothesis, or Yang-Mills existence and mass gap. Poincaré is excluded because it was already solved at the forecast date.

Forecast event: a correct complete solution to at least one of these problems, meeting its original Clay Mathematics Institute mathematical formulation, is first publicly available, and AI has contributed an identifiable new mathematical argument or proof step incorporated into that solution. Substantive human-AI collaboration qualifies. Correctness may be established by later validation; a Clay prize need not be awarded by the deadline. Partial progress alone does not qualify. Give one probability for at least one qualifying solution by each deadline; do not give separate probabilities for individual problems.

Estimate the cumulative probability of this event by each deadline. The deadlines are December 31 of 2026, 2030, 2035, 2040, and 2050. Probabilities must be numbers between 0 and 1 inclusive, nondecreasing with the deadline. Account for the possibility the event never occurs. Give your own best probability estimates despite uncertainty. Return only one JSON object with exactly the keys "2026", "2030", "2035", "2040", and "2050" and their numerical probabilities, with no markdown or explanation.
